absent: Locking discipline for control structures, timers, bitmaps, and virtual CPU state is not shown.
Side effects of async page-fault flag collection, machine-check handling, nested exit synthesis, and host transition helpers are not shown.
Numeric encodings of exit reasons, vectors, qualification fields, and control bits are not shown.
Behavior of intercepts outside the handled subset and of unconditional versus bitmap-driven paths beyond the stated dispatch is not shown.
Allocation, lifetime, and pinning rules for cached control structures, bitmaps, and log pages are not shown.

findings.text: IRQ-off exit dispatcher. When the virtual CPU is flagged as needing emulation it returns immediately without further action. Otherwise it examines the basic exit reason and forwards external interrupts, exception or NMI exits, and machine-check-during-entry exits to dedicated IRQ-off handlers; all other reasons are ignored at this stage.

IRQ-off exception triage. Page-fault exits capture and clear host async page-fault indicators into virtual CPU state. Device-not-available exits trigger early floating-point error preservation. Machine-check exits invoke host machine-check handling. The three cases are mutually exclusive and all occur before interrupts are re-enabled.

Early extended-feature error handling. On a device-not-available exit the implementation checks whether the fault is attributable to the extended-feature-disable mechanism and only in that case saves the corresponding error reporting register into guest floating-point state while still IRQ-off. This ordering prevents host activity from clobbering the value and distinguishes such faults from legacy task-switched faults.

IRQ-off external interrupt handling. The handler validates that exit information really denotes an external interrupt and aborts on mismatch. On success it brackets host entry and exit transitions around interrupt vector delivery and marks the virtual CPU as being at an instruction boundary.

Host stack pointer caching. The routine compares the supplied host stack value against the cached value in the loaded control structure and only on mismatch updates both the cache and the hardware control field. It is marked as safe to run without instrumentation.
Header inclusion guard. A single preprocessor definition prevents repeated inclusion of the VMX header within one translation unit.

Two informational warnings describe residual exposure to the L1 terminal fault side channel, one for the case where simultaneous multithreading remains enabled and one for the case where virtualization mitigation is disabled. Both advise of possible data leakage.

Memory type selection for extended page tables. Host device memory ranges always use an uncacheable type. When the virtual machine has no noncoherent DMA and requests ignoring of guest page attributes, all other ranges use writeback with an ignore-guest-attribute flag. Otherwise writeback without that flag is used.

Cacheability hazard for host device memory. Allowing the guest to access host device regions with cacheable attributes can trigger host machine checks, so the memory type logic forces such ranges to uncacheable.

Nested input-output interception decision. If the first-level control does not enable input-output bitmaps, the decision defers to the unconditional exiting control. Otherwise port number, access size, string and repeat modifiers, and immediate addressing mode are derived from the decoded instruction direction, a qualification value is assembled from those attributes, and nested bitmaps are consulted for the port range.

First half of nested instruction interception. A processor-identifier read continues execution only when nested secondary control enables the timestamp identifier feature; otherwise it raises an undefined-opcode fault without error code. Input-output instructions consult the input-output interception decision and continue when not intercepted, otherwise they request an input-output instruction exit.

Second half of nested interception plus exit synthesis. Descriptor table accesses require the descriptor secondary control and split into two exit reasons separating local and task state from global and interrupt tables. Halt and pause each require their respective primary control, with pause additionally requiring a repeat prefix and explicitly ignoring pause-loop exiting. Any other operation is unhandleable. Accepted instructions validate that decoded length is nonzero and within the architectural maximum before synthesizing a nested exit and reporting interception.

Timer migration on virtual CPU movement. When the virtual CPU is in guest mode the nested preemption timer is given a cancel attempt and only if cancellation reports an active timer is it restarted with its previous expiry in pinned absolute mode.

Trace interrupt entry. When no virtual CPU is running or the running CPU is not handling a nested nonmaskable interrupt from the guest, zero is returned so the non-trace path can use a constant-zero handler. Otherwise a performance monitoring request is queued for the virtual CPU, the trace overflow indicator in performance global status is set, and one is returned.
Nested nonmaskable-interrupt context predicate. Reports true exactly when the virtual CPU interrupt-handling marker indicates such an interrupt currently being serviced on behalf of the guest.

Small register staging structures. One holds a count plus a fixed-capacity array of load-store entries sized by the load-store limit. The other describes a user-return register with a flag controlling hardware load, a data value, and a mask.

Segment cache enumeration and trace context layout. The enumeration orders selector, base, limit, and access rights followed by a count. The trace context carries control, status, output base and mask, page-table match, and two sets of address-range endpoints sized by the address-range limit. The trace descriptor adds a control bitmask, a range count, capability words, and separate host and guest contexts.

Build-dependent capacities and bit ownership. User-return register capacity is 7 in one build variant and 4 in the other. Load-store staging holds 8 entries. Trace address ranges count 4. The page-modification log holds 512 entries with its head index at the last slot. Host-owned debug control bits consist solely of the freeze-in-management-mode bit.

Nested virtualization state. Tracks whether the first-level guest enabled virtualization and its pointer, log fullness, current and cached control structures including shadow copies, address-translation caches for those structures, synchronization and dirty flags, bitmap recalculation need, rare-state sync need, second-level control initialization, enlightened features, pending task-switch fault, second-level control, pinned host mappings for interrupt virtualization pages, posted-interrupt descriptor and notification vector, preemption timer state with deadline and expiry flags, pre-entry register snapshots for recovery and register propagation, processor identifiers, autostore slot, nested register set, management-mode save of virtualization and guest-mode flags, and optional enlightened mapping.

Per-virtual-CPU container. Embeds the generic virtual CPU and vendor extension, failure and bitmap-mode bytes, interrupt vectoring and flags, user-return register array with loaded indicator, optional 64-bit kernel segment base, speculation control, wait control, current and first-level control pointers, guest-host autoload sets and autostore set, real-mode state with segment copies, segment cache with per-field validity bitmask and cached selector-base-limit-rights entries, processor identifier, nested state, polling window and dirty flag, page-log page, host deadline timestamp, feature-control value with valid-bits mask including lock, launch-control hashes, optimization control, framebuffer-clear disable, trace and branch-record descriptors, and a page-aligned exception-information pointer.

Per-virtual-machine container. Embeds the generic virtual machine object, holds a task-state address, a flag and address for completion of the identity page table, and a table for posted-interrupt descriptors used by interprocessor-interrupt virtualization.
Register interception enabler. Unconditionally enables interception for the given register and access type by delegating to the generic intercept setter with enabling requested.

Register bitmap accessor generation. A templated helper maps low and high architectural ranges onto distinct bitmap regions with separate read and write bases and reports success for out-of-range registers. Instantiations provide test, clear, and set operations for both access types, plus a reader extracting the low byte of guest interrupt status.

Required and optional entry controls. Entry always requires loading of debug controls; the 64-bit variant additionally requires long-mode entry. Optional entry features cover performance global control, page attributes, extended feature register, bound configuration, trace pip concealment, trace control, and control-flow state.

Required and optional exit controls. Exit always requires saving debug controls and acknowledging interrupts on exit; the 64-bit variant additionally requires host address-space size selection. Optional exit features cover performance control load and save, page attribute and extended register save and load, preemption timer save, bound clearing, trace pip and control clearing, and control-flow state load.

Required and optional execution controls. Pin-based execution always requires external-interrupt masking and NMI exiting, with virtual NMIs, posted interrupts, and preemption timer as optional. Primary processor-based execution always requires exiting on halt, page-table loads and stores, unconditional input-output, debug-register moves, timestamp offsetting, wait and monitor, page invalidation, performance-counter reads, and interrupt-window opening, with one variant additionally requiring privilege-level register load-store exiting.
External bit operation relied upon when marking trace overflow status; owned elsewhere.
External timer primitive relied upon when rearming the nested preemption timer; owned elsewhere.
External arithmetic helper relied upon when validating decoded instruction length; owned elsewhere.
External bit-mask helper relied upon when assembling input-output qualification flags; owned elsewhere.
